basis: The Fed delivered the roughly 93%-priced 25 bp hike to 3.75%-4.00%; the incremental hawkish surprise was a unanimous vote and projections pointing to another 2026 hike.
Chair Warsh said the economy and labor market remain firm while inflation is too high, framing the move as removal of accommodation rather than a one-off response to oil.
Post-decision stocks pulled back, the 2-year yield and dollar rose, and VIX reached 18.50; treat the completed 5m and 15m post-Fed holds as required confirmation rather than the announcement spike.

WTI fell about 3% near 102.5 as Saudi supply rerouting and softer-than-expected inventory draws offset geopolitical risk; gold, silver, copper and Bitcoin face tighter-rate and stronger-dollar headwinds.
Natural gas retains a supply-risk bid from reduced LNG flows, but energy remains headline-sensitive and can reverse abruptly.
